title: Critical Unsloth Studio Flaw Executes Malicious Code When Users Select Hugging Face Models
content_md: A critical arbitrary code execution vulnerability in Unsloth Studio allowed malicious Hugging Face model repositories to run attacker-controlled Python code when a user merely selected a model in the interface. Unsloth fixed the issue in version 2026.6.9, and users running Studio should upgrade immediately. Researchers at Pillar Security found that the flaw affected the browser-based Studio interface included with the standard unsloth Python package. Although Studio was described as beta, the vulnerable component was delivered through normal pip install unsloth deployments, placing it within potentially sensitive AI development and fine-tuning environments. Critical Unsloth Studio Flaw The vulnerability did not require a victim to load model weights, begin inference, or intentionally enable execution of model-supplied code. Instead, selecting an attacker-controlled Hugging Face repository caused Studio’s backend to inspect the model’s config.json file. A malicious repository could include an auto_map entry in its configuration that pointed Transformers components, such as AutoConfig , to custom Python files stored in the same repository. When the backend processed that configuration with trust_remote_code=True , the Transformers library downloaded and imported the supplied Python module.
